mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Federal Funds Rate by more than 0.5% in the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last two months indicates a strong demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last two months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a slowing economy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% in the last two months, it signals strong consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it indicates inflationary pressure during a tightening cycle, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% in the last quarter and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in the last two months, it signals robust economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% in 3 months and HOUST increase > 5% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
